security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged many shell syntax examples, but review found them to be documentation samples or a safe Bash template. I found no prompt injection, hidden execution, credential exfiltration, or malicious network behavior. The /etc/passwd example should be replaced with neutral sample data to reduce false alarms and user risk.

remediation.issue: A documentation example reads /etc/passwd to show awk field separators.
remediation.suggestion: Replace it with a neutral colon-delimited sample file and avoid sensitive system paths in examples.

remediation.issue: Network examples show curl and wget commands that users may copy directly.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholder domains and add a short reminder to verify destinations before running download or HTTP commands.

remediation.issue: The references include many executable shell snippets without a global safety notice.
remediation.suggestion: State that examples should be reviewed and adapted before execution in user environments.

content.user_title: Write Safer Bash and Zsh Scripts
content.value_statement: Shell scripts often fail because of quoting, error handling, and platform differences. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for safer automation.
actual_capabilities: Explains Bash strict mode, safer word splitting, traps, and error handling.
Provides patterns for argument parsing, confirmations, logging, and usage output.
Shows safe file iteration with find, null delimiters, arrays, and globs.
Covers common text, date, JSON, network, and temporary file operations.
Includes a reusable Bash script template with dry-run and command dispatch.
Suggests modern command-line tools such as rg, fd, fzf, jq, yq, bat, and eza.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not verify scripts against a real target system.
Examples may need changes for macOS, Linux, Bash versions, or Zsh behavior.
It does not replace shellcheck, integration tests, or production review.
Network and filesystem examples should be reviewed before execution.

use_cases.title: Build Maintenance Scripts
use_cases.description: Create Bash scripts for cleanup, deployment support, log handling, and batch file processing.

use_cases.title: Debug Shell Failures
use_cases.description: Improve quoting, option parsing, error handling, and portability in existing shell scripts.

use_cases.title: Learn Safer Patterns
use_cases.description: Understand common Bash and Zsh patterns with practical examples and clear safety notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Bash script that accepts one file path, validates it, prints a clear error when missing, and uses safe quoting.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this shell script for quoting, error handling, portability, and unsafe commands. Explain each change before revising it.

prompt_templates.title: Add Batch Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Bash batch processor for a directory of text files. Include dry-run behavior, logging, cleanup, and safe file iteration.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a Production Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Bash script for command injection, race conditions, destructive operations, secret handling, and cross-platform risks.

output_examples.input: Create a script template for processing files in a directory.
output: A structured plan with strict mode, usage text, option parsing, dry-run support, logging, and cleanup traps.
A clear explanation of where to add processing logic and how errors are handled.

output_examples.input: Review a script that loops over file names with spaces.
output: A diagnosis of unsafe word splitting and missing quoting.
A safer iteration approach that handles spaces, newlines, and empty matches.

output_examples.input: Make this script work on macOS and Linux.
output: A portability review of date, stat, sed, and path handling differences.
Recommended alternatives or compatibility branches for each platform issue.

best_practices: Ask for the target shell, operating system, and failure mode before writing complex scripts.
Use strict mode, quoted variables, arrays, traps, and explicit validation by default.
Review destructive, network, and filesystem commands with extra care before suggesting execution.
anti_patterns: Do not use eval with untrusted input or build commands through unsafe string concatenation.
Do not parse ls output when globs or find can handle files safely.
Do not hide errors or delete files recursively without validation and clear user intent.

faq.question: Does this skill run shell commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to use when helping with scripts.

faq.question: Can it help with both Bash and Zsh?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Bash patterns and includes a section for Zsh-specific features.

faq.question: Does it include a full script template?
faq.answer: Yes. The reference template includes strict mode, logging, option parsing, command dispatch, cleanup, and dry-run support.

faq.question: Can it replace shellcheck?
faq.answer: No. It can guide improvements, but shellcheck and tests should still validate scripts.

faq.question: Is it useful for production automation?
faq.answer: Yes, when paired with review, testing, and environment-specific validation before execution.

faq.question: What security topics does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers quoting, input validation, temporary files, destructive commands, secrets, race conditions, and command injection risks.
